fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`caused_by` is the only machine-readable causation edge in the store, and it is not
trustworthy today. `rebar link <bug> <target> caused_by` accepts ANY target: there is no
check that the target is a change at all. The most-linked target in the current store is a
misattribution whose "children" are unrelated CI items, so `rebar metrics`
(`bug_caused_by_fan_in`, `rebar/metrics/bug_trends.py`) and the epic-close `caused_by` floor
(`rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py`) both reason over edges nobody validated.

Verified against the tree at `origin/main` before writing this plan:

* `rebar link` has NO validation beyond relation grammar, cycles, the redundant-link guard
  and the closed-source guard (`rebar/graph/_links.py:add_dependency`), and NO `--force`
  flag (`rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:build_link` exposes only `--dry-run`).
* `add_dependency` ALREADY carries a relation-specific target rule — `depends_on` refuses a
  closed target — so a `caused_by` target rule is the same shape, not a new concept.
* The "does a commit reference this ticket?" scan exists exactly once, privately, as
  `_referencing_commits` in `rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`. It walks `git log` (HEAD,
  not `origin/main`) and resolves each `rebar-ticket:`/subject ref through the shared
  resolver. Its `[]` return conflates "scanned, none found" with "no git history".
* The bug-close path (`transition_close._apply_caused_by`) writes its blame-derived edge via
  `graph._links._write_link_event`, deliberately bypassing `add_dependency`; it is
  best-effort and out of scope here.

## Approach

One shared scan, two consumers — the epic's shared-module shape.

1. Hoist the trailer/subject scan into the existing shared module
   `rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py` as `referencing_commits(ids, tracker, repo_root)`,
   returning `list[str] | None` where `None` means "git history could not be read" — the same
   `None`-vs-`[]` distinction `changed_paths` in that module already uses.
   `close_precheck._referencing_commits` becomes a thin `... or []` delegate, so the close
   gate's behaviour is unchanged by construction.
2. Refuse an unverifiable `caused_by` at link time in `composer.link_core`
   (`rebar/_commands/link_revert.py`) — the ONE seam the library, CLI and MCP all route
   through, so parity is structural rather than triplicated. The rule: the RESOLVED TARGET
   must have at least one commit referencing it. Targeting the ticket itself (not its
   descendants) is deliberate: `caused_by` should name the specific change that introduced
   the defect, and crediting an epic's children is the misattribution shape this story exists
   to stop. `caused_by` is never hierarchy-promoted, so the resolved target is the requested
   one.
3. Unverifiable is NOT invalid: when the scan returns `None` (no code repo / no commits) the
   link is allowed. A refusal must mean "this target has no commit", never "this clone has no
   history".
4. Escape hatch: `--force[=<reason>]` on the CLI, `force=` on the library and MCP surfaces,
   spelled exactly as `claim --force`. Its parser is hoisted to
   `_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:extract_force` and `claim._parse_force` delegates to it, so
   the spelling has one implementation rather than a third copy. `link --dry-run` previews
   the refusal instead of "Would create".

## Scope

`src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`,
`src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py`,
`src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt`, `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py`,
`src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`,
`tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py` (new), `tests/interfaces/adapters.py`,
`tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py`, `docs/ticket-model.md`,
`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`.

## Explicitly OUT of scope

The original plan's `introducing_sha` schema field + `rebar fsck` date check, and the
"attach the 196-row dated corpus" criterion, are cut and re-filed as a follow-up linked
`discovered_from`. Reasons: (a) no surface writes `introducing_sha`, so the field would land
dead; (b) `fsck` is a STORE-integrity walker (`_commands/fsck.py` dispatches only tracker
checks) and must run where no code repo exists, so a git-history check is the wrong home;
(c) the corpus is a review artifact that does not exist in the repo.

## Testing

New `tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py` (store with real commits):

* happy path — `caused_by` to a target carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer commit succeeds;
* refusal — `caused_by` to a commit-less target raises, names the target and `--force`, and
  writes NO edge (`show_ticket(...)["deps"]` unchanged);
* `force="..."` on the same input succeeds and records the edge;
* other relations (`relates_to`, `blocks`) to the same commit-less target are unaffected;
* unverifiable — a store whose code repo has no commits allows the link;
* delegation — `close_precheck._referencing_commits` still returns `[]`, not `None`, when
  history is unreadable.

Pinning (must pass unchanged): `tests/unit/test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py`,
`tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate*.py`,
`tests/unit/test_claim*.py`, `tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `caused_by` link to a commit-less target is refused identically on library, CLI and
      MCP, and `force` bypasses it on all three; checked by two new rows in the write-parity
      oracle: `pytest tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py -q`.
- [ ] Refusal names the target and the escape hatch and leaves the store unwritten; the
      unverifiable-store case is allowed; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py -q`.
- [ ] The scan has ONE implementation and the close gate is behaviour-identical; checked by
      `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py -q`
      plus `grep -c 'git.*log.*%H' src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` returning 0.
- [ ] Gates green: `make lint && make typecheck && python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      reports `new=0 increased=0`.
fields.title: Refuse a caused_by link whose target has no referencing commit
